title: Which AI + Game Engine Would You Recommend for Someone With Limited Time?
author: Palacinkarina
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I work a full-time job, so I don’t have enough free time to learn and do every part of game development myself. I have a lot of game ideas I’d love to bring to life, and with today’s AI tools, I’m wondering how far I could realistically get with AI doing most of the coding and technical work.

What engine would you recommend for this, Unity, Unreal, Godot, or something else?

And which AI tools are actually worth paying for? I’m fine with spending money if the difference is significant.

I’d love to hear your current setup, especially:

• Which engine?

• Which AI?

• Monthly cost?

• How much of the coding/work does it handle for you?

• What has been the best value for you?

I’m not looking for a shortcut where I press a button and get a finished game. I’m willing to learn and work on it, I simply need AI to handle a large part of the technical workload because of my limited free time.

Thanks!

replies.author: tabaxi_gf
replies.body: Can you get any more specific than that?  You can also do that just with HTML 5 if you want, claude or codex will happily generate that for you and you don’t need to use an engine.

replies.author: StretchedNut
replies.body: Just a heads up, incremental and idle games are super oversaturated right now as everyone is making them. Everyone is also trying to use AI to make games for them with no experience. Not saying you shouldn’t do it, just thought I’d let you know so you can manage expectations

comments.author: LazyAp3
comments.body: Godot and vs code with codex works great, you can use chat gpt to chat about what you want and let it design an agent and the prompts to push into codex, if you dont go with "i want game xy with feature a,b,c and style z, go!" and work in smaller segments you can make progress that works and doesnt break after every new addition really fast, pair that with a clean github workflow and you are golden, it all heavily depends on the scope of your game though and also your understanding of gamedesign and how you handle your assets/art

comments.author: Jolly_Roger-99
comments.body:
I learned that assets are the hard part. Godot and the AI godot Plugin (MCP Server, which give the AI all tools the Engine have) and cursor for coding works very well. 

My Prototype is working and make fun after a few weeks, but to get a good looking map, or the Units is a totaly different thing. 

Until now i did not found  1 AI tool that makes good assets.

comments.author: DeniedWorks
comments.body:
Unity and ChatGPT Astra. I say these two for you specifically as you are in a similar situation to me. The advantage of Unity is the marketplace for me and you will get much more usage out of Astra than you will with Claude’s Fable and that has been the case for a while. Assuming you use both on high (I have both max personal subscriptions for both). 

Astra can help you make graphics very easily and well made as well as some basic 3D models and use the computer better and more efficiently. Its coding capabilities are on par with Fable 5, which 95% of the time is great. Fable 5.1 is better at coding and frontend design in my opinion. 

With Unity and Codex it is really easy to add multiplayer with something like SpacetimeDB honestly extremely easily. Godot and Unity both being C# will help the models out vs C++ in unreal engine.

comments.author: Dr_Judge_Esquire_Jr
comments.body: Godot and Claude. Get the Godot MCP too. When you start getting into much more complex mechanics you might want to also involve Astra but fable/opus can handle so much.

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
Godot
Codex 
20-200$
All of it
Astra model

If you truly want to build a game, there are no shortcuts, especially if you don't know what you are doing and have to learn everything. I started about 100000 projects before I finally found a game idea that stuck. The experience from all projects before is the part that made my game possible.

comments.author: RoryOS
comments.body:
I'm using Godot and Claude, the free version. 

Making use of a project with a context library is what I do but the mcp thing is meant to be very good. 

I'm not willing to learn to code. I've tried, multiple times and have cobbled code together in the past. But it's not for me. I'm nearly 40, just having some fun for myself in my very limited spare time. That said, I think my attempts from the past 20-25 years of on and off messing about with game engines had helped me steer the AI and fix up it's mistakes. 

I'm wildly impressed with the latest batch of free models. I have been able to work on a dream project I never thought I'd manage to make

comments.author: Legitimate-Paint2165
comments.body: $20 ChatGPT connected to GitHub gives you the ability to edit your project from work on your phone with Sol. Save work mode for Codex with Astra for more difficult things.
